meta.titolo: Rymembra — free music player for Windows: FLAC, gapless, even loudness
meta.descrizione: Free, open-source music player for Windows. Gapless FLAC and MP3 at even loudness, playlists from your Spotify data, and the missing tracks from free catalogs.
meta.immagine: Rymembra, a music player for Windows

hero.lede: Rymembra is a free music player for Windows. It plays the files already on your disk, rebuilds your playlists — even from your Spotify data — and looks for the missing tracks only where it's allowed to.
hero.nota: Free and open source, MIT licence. Windows 64-bit, version {versione}, released {data}.
hero.alt: Rymembra's home screen, with this week's collections, the track to resume and the queue
hero.didascalia: The home screen: this week's collections, the interrupted track ready to resume where it stopped, and the queue on the right. The pictures show the Italian interface; the program speaks English too.

altrove.testo: Rymembra is a program for Windows: send yourself the link and download it on your PC.

viaggio.testo: From a line in a playlist to your speakers: what Rymembra does, one step at a time.

playlist.testo: Ask Spotify for a copy of your data and you get a ZIP file: playlists, liked songs, saved albums, followed artists and years of listening history. Rymembra reads it on your computer, all at once — nothing leaves the machine.
punti: An M3U, M3U8 or PLS file works too.
So does a link to a track, an album or a collection on archive.org or audius.co — no account, no API key.

disco.titolo: First, it looks on your disk.
disco.testo: Every track is matched against the library Rymembra keeps of your music folders, by its tags and its duration, album by album. What you already own is found and played from where it is.
punti: Folders watch themselves: copy an album in, and seconds later it's in the library.
On a NAS or a mapped drive, a share that doesn't answer for a moment makes tracks unverified, never gone.
A scan that would remove many tracks shows them to you and asks first.

cataloghi.titolo: What's missing, it looks for where it's allowed.
cataloghi.testo: The Internet Archive and Audius hold music published to be shared: more than 250,000 concerts on the Live Music Archive, netlabels, the public domain, tracks that artists released under open licences. A track is downloaded only when its own licence allows it, and it keeps that licence. When no studio version is free, a concert can stand in — and the track says it's live.
cataloghi.acquisti: No free source carries the commercial catalog, and Rymembra won't fetch it from where it shouldn't: what it can't find lawfully goes on a shopping list, with links to Bandcamp and Qobuz.
cataloghi.esclusi: Left out on purpose: YouTube, whose terms forbid downloading and storing its content, and Spotify's private endpoints, which would mean unauthorized access.
cataloghi.alt: The settings card that lists where the music comes from
cataloghi.didascalia: Settings, «Where the music comes from»: every source with the rule it follows.

suono.titolo: Then it plays, the way it should.
suono.testo: Every track at the same loudness: Rymembra measures each file with EBU R128 while nothing is playing, and never raises a track past its own peak. Albums play without gaps, even when a 44.1 kHz record meets a 48 kHz sound card. And a line under the title says what the file really is, as the decoder reads it.
punti: Equalizer, crossfade and a queue that survives a restart.
Synced lyrics from LRCLIB, and a way to time them yourself.
suono.alt: The now-playing screen with the spectrum analyzer
suono.didascalia: Now playing, with the spectrum scene and the line that says what the file is. [How the audio engine works]({base}docs/audio/).

skin.titolo: It looks the way you want.
skin.testo: A skin can repaint and animate any of the 101 parts of the window — colors, type, borders, motion — and its contrast is checked before you share it. The built-in Studio edits skins on the program's real pages, and can ask a language model, on your machine or remote, to make the change for you.
skin.altStudio: The Studio, the built-in skin editor
skin.didascaliaStudio: The Studio: layers on the left, the program's real pages in the middle, the inspector on the right.
skin.altPlain: The album grid with the Plain skin
skin.altNeon: The same album grid with the Neon skin
skin.didascalia: The same albums in Plain, the default skin, and in Neon. Only the skin changes.

tuo.testo: No account, no telemetry, no Rymembra server. The library lives in a database on your computer: tags found online and your own corrections go there, never into your music files.
punti: Back up and sync through a shared folder — Syncthing, OneDrive, Dropbox — or through Google Drive with a Google project of your own.
The whole profile fits in one .ryprofile file you can carry by hand.
Every network request the program can make is listed in [PRIVACY.md]({privacy}).

scena.stessoVolume: Every track brought to the same loudness
scena.senzaPause: One track ends, the next begins: no gap

scarica.testo: One installer for Windows 64-bit. Updates arrive by themselves, signed, and install only when you say so.
scarica.file: The file is `{file}`, released {data}. [What's new]({note}), [all versions]({tutte}).

impronta.verifica: To check the file, in PowerShell: `Get-FileHash $HOME\Downloads\{file}` must print the same checksum.

passo1.testo: It's a single installer. If the previous version is installed, it replaces it.

passo2.testo: The installer isn't signed with a certificate, which costs money every year, so Windows warns you the first time. Click «More info», then «Run anyway».

passo3.testo: Choose your music folder. A short tour shows you around once, on the real window.

scarica.precedente: Coming from Aether, the program's previous name? The installer replaces it, and on first start your library, settings, skins and accounts carry over by themselves. Nothing is overwritten.

smartscreen.testo: Microsoft Defender SmartScreen prevented an unrecognized app from starting. Running this app might put your PC at risk.

elenco.r: Yes, and it will stay free. There's no paid version and none is planned: two of its sources, the Live Music Archive and Jamendo, have non-commercial clauses that a paid version would break. Development is funded by donations.

elenco.d: Does it run on macOS or Linux?
elenco.r: Not today. The installer is for Windows only, and there's no macOS, Linux or mobile version yet.

elenco.d: Why does Windows warn me when I install it?
elenco.r: Because the installer isn't signed with a code-signing certificate, which needs an identity check and a yearly fee. SmartScreen stops unsigned programs it hasn't seen often: click «More info», then «Run anyway». Updates are a different matter: the program verifies their signature before installing anything.

elenco.d: Where does the music come from? Is it legal?
elenco.r: From your own files first. Then from the Internet Archive and Audius, and only when a track's licence allows a copy; every track keeps its licence, and the Live Music Archive's non-commercial clause binds you too. Rymembra doesn't download from YouTube and doesn't scrape Spotify. The details are in [TERMS.md]({termini}).

elenco.d: Will it change my music files?
elenco.r: No. Tags found online, your corrections, covers, lyrics, plays and ratings live in the library database. The only things written into a music folder are the tracks you download and, if you turn it on, a .lrc lyrics file beside a track.

elenco.d: Can I bring my Spotify playlists?
elenco.r: Yes. Ask Spotify for your data from your account's privacy page: it arrives as a ZIP, usually within days, and the full listening history takes longer. Rymembra reads it on your computer and matches each track against your library and the free catalogs. The ZIP holds no audio: what you don't own and no free catalog has goes on the shopping list.

elenco.d: Does it send my data anywhere?
elenco.r: There's no telemetry and no Rymembra server. The program only talks to the services you use — the catalogs, MusicBrainz for tags, LRCLIB for lyrics, GitHub to check for updates, and whatever you connect yourself. [PRIVACY.md]({privacy}) lists every request and what it sends.

sostieni.titolo: Free, and kept going by the people who use it.
sostieni.testo: If Rymembra is useful to you, a donation keeps it going. A bug report or an idea helps just as much.
